chunks: ‘Abdullah ibn Ibrahim ibn Ali ibn Abdullah ibn Ja‘far ibn Abi Talib narrated to me, from Yazid ibn Salit al-Zaydi, Abu al-Hakam said; and ‘Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Umarah al-Jarmi informed me, from Yazid ibn Salit, who said:

I met Abū Ibrāhīm (عليه السلام) while we were intending to perform ‘Umrah, at a place along the road. I said: “May I be made your ransom, do you recognize this place where we are?” He said: “Yes; do you recognize it too?” I said: “Yes. My father and I met you here while you were with Abū ‘Abdillāh (عليه السلام), and your brothers were with him. My father said to him: ‘May my father and mother be your ransom, all of you are purified Imams, and no one is free from death. So tell me something which I may relate to the one who will succeed me after me, so that he may not go astray.’”

He said: “Yes, O Abū ‘Abdillāh, these are my children, and this one is their master,” and he pointed to you. “He has been taught judgment, understanding, generosity, and knowledge of what people need and of what they differ about in the affairs of their religion and their worldly life. In him are good character and good response, and he is a gate from the gates of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and in him is another quality better than all of that.” My father said to him: “What is it? May my father and mother be your ransom.” He (عليه السلام) said: “Allah, Mighty and Majestic, shall bring forth from him the relief of this Ummah, its succor, its banner, its light, its excellence, and its wisdom. He is the best newborn and the best youth. Through him Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will spare bloodshed, reconcile estrangement, gather what is scattered, mend what is split, clothe the naked, feed the hungry, give security to the fearful, send down rain, and show mercy to the servants. He is the best mature man and the best youth. His speech is judgment and his silence is knowledge. He clarifies for the people that wherein they differ, and he will lead his clan before the time of his maturity.” My father said to him: “May my father and mother be your ransom, has he been born?” He said: “Yes, and years have passed over him.”

Yazīd said: Then someone came to us such that we could not speak in his presence. Yazīd said: So I said to Abū Ibrāhīm (عليه السلام): “Then you inform me with the like of what your father (عليه السلام) informed me.” He said to me: “Yes. My father (عليه السلام) was in a time that was not this time.” I said to him: “So whoever among you is satisfied with only this, then upon him be the curse of Allah.” He said: Abū Ibrāhīm laughed intensely, then said: “I shall inform you, O Abū ‘Umārah.”

“I left my house and made an outward وصية to one of my sons, and I associated my other sons with him in the outward matter; but inwardly I made the bequest to him alone and singled him out. Had the matter been left to me, I would have placed it in al-Qāsim my son because of my love for him and my compassion toward him; but that belongs to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, who places it where He wills. The Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) came to me with news of him, then showed him to me and showed me those who would be with him. Thus none of us is designated until the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) and my grandfather ‘Alī, may the blessings of Allah be upon him, come with the news of him. And I saw with the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) a ring, a sword, a staff, a book, and a turban.”

I said: “What are these, O Messenger of Allah?” He said to me: “As for the turban, it is the authority of Allah, Mighty and Majestic; as for the sword, it is the might of Allah, Blessed and Exalted; as for the book, it is the light of Allah, Blessed and Exalted; as for the staff, it is the power of Allah; and as for the ring, it gathers all these matters.” Then he said to me: “The command has gone from you to another than you.” I said: “O Messenger of Allah, show him to me; which one of them is he?” The Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) said: “I have not seen among the Imams anyone more distressed at the separation from this command than you. Had the Imamate been by love, Ismā‘īl would have been more beloved to your father than you; but that is from Allah, Mighty and Majestic.”

Then Abū Ibrāhīm said: “I saw all my children, the living among them and the dead. Amīr al-Mu’minīn (عليه السلام) said to me: ‘This one is their master,’ and he pointed to my son ‘Alī. ‘So he is from me and I am from him, and Allah is with the doers of good.’” Yazīd said: Then Abū Ibrāhīm (عليه السلام) said: “O Yazīd, this is a trust with you, so do not inform anyone of it except one who is intelligent or a servant whom you know to be truthful; and if you are asked about the testimony, then testify to it.”
And it is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “Indeed Allah commands you to deliver trusts to their أهل.”
And He also said to us: “And who is more unjust than one who conceals a testimony he has from Allah?”

He said: Then Abū Ibrāhīm (عليه السلام) said: “So I turned to the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) and said: ‘You have gathered them for me; may my father and mother be your ransom, so which one of them is he?’ He said: ‘He is the one who sees by the light of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, hears with understanding, and speaks with wisdom. He is correct and does not err; he knows and is not ignorant, taught judgment and knowledge. He is this one,’ and he took the hand of my son ‘Alī.”

Then he said: “How little your stay with him will be. When you return from your journey, then make your وصية, set your affair in order, and finish what you intend, for you will be departing from them and dwelling with others than them. When you wish, call ‘Alī, and let him wash you and shroud you, for that is purity for you, and nothing is proper except that; and that is a sunnah that has already passed. Then lie down before him, arrange his brothers and his paternal uncles behind him, and command him to pronounce nine takbīrs over you. Thus his designation and authority over you will have been established while you are still alive. Then gather your children for him after them, make them witness against it, and call Allah, Mighty and Majestic, as witness; and Allah suffices as a witness.”

Yazīd said: Then Abū Ibrāhīm (عليه السلام) said to me: “I shall be seized in this year, and the command belongs to my son ‘Alī, the namesake of ‘Alī and ‘Alī. As for the first ‘Alī, he is ‘Alī ibn Abī Ṭālib; and as for the latter, he is ‘Alī ibn al-Ḥusayn (عليه السلام). He has been given the understanding of the first, his forbearance, his support, his affection, his religion, and his trial; and the trial of the latter and his patience over what he dislikes. He is not to speak except four years after the death of Hārūn.”

Then he said to me: “O Yazīd, when you pass by this place and meet him—and you shall meet him—then give him glad tidings that there will be born to him a trustworthy, secure, blessed boy. He will inform you that you have indeed met me. At that time tell him that the slave-woman from whom this boy will be is a slave-woman from the household of Māriyah, the slave-woman of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), the mother of Ibrāhīm. If you are able to convey my salām to her, then do so.”

Yazīd said: After the passing of Abū Ibrāhīm (عليه السلام), I met ‘Alī (عليه السلام), and he initiated me, saying: “O Yazīd, what do you say regarding ‘Umrah?” I said: “May my father and mother be your ransom, that is up to you, and I do not have the expenses.” He said: “Glory be to Allah! Were we ever to burden you and not suffice you?” So we went out until we came to that place. He initiated me and said: “O Yazīd, this is a place where you have often met your neighbors and your paternal uncles.” I said: “Yes.” Then I related the report to him, and he said to me: “As for the slave-woman, she has not yet arrived. When she comes, I will convey to her his salām.” We then went on to Makkah, and he purchased her in that year. She did not remain long before conceiving and giving birth to that boy.

Yazīd said: The brothers of ‘Alī had hoped to inherit from him, so his brothers showed hostility to me without any wrongdoing on my part. Then Isḥāq ibn Ja‘far said to them: “By Allah, I have seen him, and he indeed used to sit with Abū Ibrāhīm in the place in which I myself would not sit.”

key_terms.أَئِمَّةٌ: divinely designated Imams who lead the community
key_terms.الشَّهَادَةِ: testimony that must be upheld truthfully
key_terms.الْأَمَانَاتِ: trusts that must be returned to their rightful people
key_terms.الْأَمْرُ: the command or authority of the Imamate
key_terms.بَابٌ مِنْ أَبْوَابِ اللَّهِ: a divinely appointed means through which guidance is accessed
key_terms.وَدِيعَةٌ: a trust entrusted for preservation and proper delivery

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the designation of Imam al-Rida (عليه السلام) and the transmission of the Imamate?
ai.summary: This hadith is a detailed narrative of explicit indications toward the Imamate of Imam al-Rida (عليه السلام), conveyed through Yazid ibn Salit from Imam al-Kazim (عليه السلام) and earlier from Imam al-Sadiq (عليه السلام). It describes the divinely designated nature of the Imamate, the transmission of authority through the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), and instructions regarding testimony, trust, and succession among the Ahl al-Bayt (عليهم السلام).

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Mihran, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Abu Al Hakam Al Armany who said, ‘Abdullah Bin Ibrahim Bin Ali Bin Abdullah Bin Ja’far Bin Abu Talib, from Yazeed Bin Saley Al Zaydi who said, ‘Abu Al Hakam said and Abdullah Bin Muhammad Bin Umara Al Jarmy informed me, from Yazeed Bin Saleyt who said, 
‘I met Abu Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup> in one of the roads and we intended (performance of) Umrah. So I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>!

Do you realise this place which we are in?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, so do you realise it (as well)?’ I said, ‘Yes, because I and my father, we met you<sup>asws</sup>, we met you<sup>asws</sup> over here and you<sup>asws</sup> were with Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, and with him<sup>asws</sup> were your<sup>asws</sup> brothers. So my father said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May my father and my mother die for you! You<sup>asws</sup> are all Purified Imams<sup>asws</sup>, and the death, no one is immune from it. So if there occurs an occurrence (of death) to me, whom would my descendants refer to after me so that they do not stray?’ 
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, O Abdullah!

These are my<sup>asws</sup> children and this one<sup>asws</sup> is their chief’, and he<sup>asws</sup> gestured towards you<sup>asws</sup>, and he<sup>asws</sup> is known for the judgements, and the understanding, and the generosity, and the recognition of what the people would be needy to him<sup>asws</sup> for, and what they are differing in from the matters of their Religion and their world, and in him<sup>asws</sup> are the good morals, and the good answers, and he<sup>asws</sup> is a door from the doors of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic, and in him<sup>asws</sup> is other, better than all of this’. 
So my father said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘And what is it? May my father and my mother be (sacrificed) for you<sup>asws</sup>!’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic would Bring about from him<sup>asws</sup>, the relief of this community, and its blossoms, and its banners, and its light, and its merits, and its wisdom. He<sup>azwj</sup> would have the best of ‘مَوْلُودٍ’ (coming to world) and the best of the growths. Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic would Save the blood by him<sup>asws</sup> and Reconcile by him<sup>asws</sup> between two parties, and Gather by him<sup>asws</sup> the diversities, and Bridge by him<sup>asws</sup> the rifts, and Clothe by him<sup>asws</sup> the bare, and Feed by him<sup>asws</sup> the hungry, and Secure by him<sup>asws</sup> the fearful, and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Send down the drops (rain) due to him<sup>asws</sup>, and have Mercy on the servants due to him<sup>asws</sup>.
He<sup>asws</sup> would be the best of the elderly and the best of the budding (youths). His<sup>asws</sup> words would be wisdom and his<sup>asws</sup> silence - the knowledge. He<sup>asws</sup> would clarify to the people whatever they would be differing in, and he<sup>asws</sup> would be assisting his<sup>asws</sup> claim from before his<sup>asws</sup> attainment of the adulthood’.

So my father said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May my father and my mother be (sacrificed) for you<sup>asws</sup>! And has he<sup>asws</sup> been born yet?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, and years have passed’. 
Yazeed said, ‘So there came to us one who we did not have the leeway of speaking (in his presence)’. Yazeed said, ‘Then I said to Abu Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>), ‘So (now) you<sup>asws</sup> inform me with similar to what your<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> informed me with’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Yes. My<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> was in an era, (but) this isn’t his<sup>asws</sup> era’. So I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘So whoever is pleased from you<sup>asws</sup> with this (much only), so upon him is the Curse of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’. So Abu Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup> laughed intensely, then said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> shall inform you, O Abu Umara!

I<sup>asws</sup> came out from my<sup>asws</sup> house, so I<sup>asws</sup> bequeathed to my<sup>asws</sup> son<sup>asws</sup> so and so, and I<sup>asws</sup> participated with him<sup>asws</sup> my<sup>asws</sup> (other) sons regarding the apparent, and I<sup>asws</sup> bequeathed to him<sup>asws</sup> in the hidden, alone, and had the matter been to me<sup>asws</sup>, I<sup>asws</sup> would have made it to be in Al-Qasim, my<sup>asws</sup> son, due to my<sup>asws</sup> love for him and my<sup>asws</sup> kindness upon him. But, that is up to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic. He<sup>azwj</sup> Makes it to be wherever He<sup>azwj</sup> so Desires to. 
And Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> had come to me<sup>asws</sup> with his<sup>asws</sup> news, then he<sup>saww</sup> showed him<sup>asws</sup> to me<sup>asws</sup>, and I<sup>asws</sup> saw the ones who would be with him<sup>asws</sup>. And like that it is. Not one of us<sup>asws</sup> can be bequeath until Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> comes with his<sup>asws</sup> news, and my<sup>asws</sup> grandfather<sup>asws</sup> Ali<sup>asws</sup>.

And I<sup>asws</sup> saw with Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, his<sup>saww</sup> ring, and his<sup>saww</sup> sword, and his<sup>saww</sup> staff, and his<sup>saww</sup> Book, and his<sup>saww</sup> turban. 
So I<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What is this, O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>?’ So he<sup>saww</sup> said to me: ‘As for the turban, so it is the Authority of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic, and as for the sword, so it is the Might of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High, and as for the Book, so it is the Light of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High, and as for the Staff, so it is the Strength of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and as for the ring, so it is the entirety of these matters’. 
Then he<sup>saww</sup> said to me: ‘And the command (Imamate) has come out from you<sup>asws</sup> to other than you<sup>asws</sup>’. So I<sup>asws</sup> said, ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! Show me<sup>asws</sup>, which of them is he<sup>asws</sup>?’ So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘I<sup>saww</sup> have not seen anyone from the Imams<sup>asws</sup> anyone more apprehensive upon the separation of this command than you<sup>asws</sup>, and had the Imamate been with the love, it was so that Ismail was more beloved to your<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> than you<sup>asws</sup> were, but that is from Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic’.

Then Abu Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And I<sup>asws</sup> saw my<sup>asws</sup> children altogether, the living ones from them and the deceased. So Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘This one is their chief’, and he<sup>asws</sup> gestured towards my<sup>asws</sup> son<sup>asws</sup> Ali<sup>asws</sup>, ‘So he<sup>asws</sup> is from me<sup>asws</sup> and I<sup>asws</sup> am from him<sup>asws</sup>, and Allah<sup>asws</sup> is with the good doers’.
Yazeed said, ‘Then Abu Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Yazeed!

It is a deposit with you, therefore do not inform with it to anyone except an intellectual, or a servants whose sincerity you recognise, and if you are asked about the witnessing, so testify with it, and these are the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [4:58] Surely Allah Commands you to make over trusts to their owners.

And Heazwj Said to us as well [2:140] And who is more unjust than he who conceals a testimony that he has from Allah?’ He (the narrator) said, ‘So Abu Ibrahimasws said: ‘So Iasws turned towards Rasool-Allahazwj, and Iasws said: ‘Yousaww have gathered them for measws.

By my<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> and my<sup>asws</sup> mother, so which of them is he<sup>asws</sup>?’ So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘He<sup>asws</sup> is the one who looks by the Light of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic, and he<sup>asws</sup> hears by His<sup>azwj</sup> Understanding, and he<sup>asws</sup> speaks by His<sup>azwj</sup> Wisdom. He<sup>asws</sup> gets its right and he<sup>asws</sup> does not err, and he<sup>asws</sup> knows and he<sup>asws</sup> is not ignorant. He<sup>asws</sup> is Taught the Wisdom and the Knowledge. He<sup>asws</sup> is this one’, and he<sup>saww</sup> grabbed the hand of Ali<sup>asws</sup>, my<sup>asws</sup> son<sup>asws</sup>’.

Then hesaww said: ‘How little is yourasws remaining with himasws. So when youasws return from yourasws journey, so bequeath, and correct yourasws affairs, and be free from whatever you want, so youasws would be transferring from them and be in the vicinity of other than them. So whenever youasws want, so call Aliasws, so let himasws wash youasws, and let himasws enshroud youasws, for it would be cleaner for youasws, and nothing is straight except for that, and that is a Sunnah of the past. Then recline in front of himasws, and form rows of hisasws brothers behind him, and hisasws being a prayer leader, and instruct himasws, so let him exclaim Takbeer upon youasws, nine (exclamations), so it would he established yourasws bequest and yourasws Guardian, while youasws are alive. Then gather yourasws sons for himasws, from after himasws, so get them to bear witness, and keep Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic as a Witness, and Allahazwj Suffices as a Witness’.

Yazeed said, ‘Then Abu Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> would be Taken during this year and the command (Imamate), it would be with my<sup>asws</sup> son<sup>asws</sup> Ali<sup>asws</sup>. He<sup>asws</sup> was named by Ali<sup>asws</sup> and Ali<sup>asws</sup>. So as for the first Ali<sup>asws</sup>, so it is Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Abu Talib<sup>asws</sup>, and as for the other Ali<sup>asws</sup>, so it is Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>. He<sup>asws</sup> has been Given the understanding of the first one, and his<sup>asws</sup> forbearance, and his<sup>asws</sup> victory, and his<sup>asws</sup> cordiality, and his<sup>asws</sup> Religion, and his<sup>asws</sup> loved, and his<sup>asws</sup> ordeals and the ordeals of the other, and his<sup>asws</sup> patience upon what he<sup>asws</sup> dislikes, and it isn’t for him<sup>asws</sup> that he<sup>asws</sup> speaks except after the death of Haroun (Al-Rashid the Caliph) by four years’. 
Then, he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘O Yazeed!

And when you pass by this place and meet him<sup>asws</sup>, and you shall be meeting him<sup>asws</sup>, so give him<sup>asws</sup> the glad tidings that a boy would be born unto him<sup>asws</sup> trustworthy, secure, Blessed, and he<sup>asws</sup> would be letting you know that you had met me<sup>asws</sup>. So inform him<sup>asws</sup> during that, that the slave girl which this boy would happen to be from, is a slave girl from the Household of Maria (the Coptic), the slave girl of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, the mother of Ibrahim<sup>as</sup> (son<sup>as</sup> of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>). So if you are able to deliver the greetings from me<sup>asws</sup>, then do so’.

Yazeed said, ‘So I saw Ali<sup>asws</sup> after the passing away of Abu Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> initiated me by saying to me: ‘O Yazeed! What are you saying regarding (performing) the Umra?’ So I said, ‘By my father and my mother being for you<sup>asws</sup>! That is up to you<sup>asws</sup>, and there is no expenditure money with me’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Glory be to Allah<sup>azwj</sup>!  We<sup>asws</sup> would not encumber you and not suffice you’. So we went out until we ended up to that very place. So he<sup>asws</sup> initiated me saying, ‘O Yaeed!  This place is where you frequently meet your neighbours and your uncles in’. I said, ‘Yes’. 
Then I related the news upon him<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘As for the slave girl, so she has not come yet. So when she does come, deliver to her the greetings from him<sup>asws</sup>’. So we went to Makkah and acquired her during that year. So she did not remain except for a little before she started expecting and gave birth to that boy.

Yazeed said, ‘And it was so that the brothers of Ali<sup>asws</sup> were hoping to inherit him<sup>asws</sup>, so his<sup>asws</sup> brothers were hostile to me with any sin (wrongdoing from me). So Is’haq Bin Ja’far said to them, ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! I have seen him and he used to (make) him (sit) near to Abu Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup> in the gathering which I could not sit it’.
en.sarwar: “The the Imam (a.s.) said, “O Yazid, when ever you will pass through this place and meet and you will soon meet himgive him the glad news of the birth of trust worthy son to him, a protected and holy one. He will inform you of your meeting with me. You then inform him that the girl from whom this boy will be born is a girl from the family of Mary (Maria), the maiden girl of the Messenger of Allah, mother of Ibrahim. If will be able to convey my greetings to her you may do so.”

Yazid has said, “After the death of abu Ibrahim I met Ali (al-Rida) (a.s.) and he began to speak to me.” He said, “O Yazid, “What do you say about performing ‘Umra (visit to Makka out of Hajj season)?” I said, “May Allah take my soul and the souls of my parents in service for your cause, it is up to you. I do not have the means to journey.” The Imam (a.s.) said, “Glory belongs to Allah, We would not have asked you without first taking the rsponsibility for your exoenses.” We then left for ‘Umra until we reached that place. The Imam (a.s.) began to speak and he said, “This is the place wherein you would meet your neighbors and uncles very often.” I said, “Yes, it is true and then I related to him the story.” He then said to me, “The girl has not come as yet. When she will come I will convey his greetings to her.” Then we left for Makka and he bought her that year. Shortly afterwards she give borth to the that boy.”

Yazid has said, “Brothers of Ali (al-Rida) wanted to have a part in the leadership and they became my enemies for no good reason. Ishaq ibn Ja‘far told them, by Allah, I have seen him sit so near to abu Ibrahim that even I could sit so close.”
